title: CI run recovery recipes
text: When a QA case attaches to a CI run it names the run, then teaches only registered commands: `yoke github-actions failed-log` for each failed job and `yoke github-actions run cancel` to cancel. The failed-log report prefers pytest FAILURES / ERRORS and Vitest Failed Tests / Failed Suites sections over trailing error annotations; bounded test regions keep their first failure and summary. Each job gets an equal share of the CLI human-read byte limit after headers, labels, URLs, trim notices and a warning margin are reserved; --full still writes complete logs to local files. Without a test section, it prefers the last nonzero process-exit annotation over later failure-reporting annotations, then falls back to the last error annotation so recovered early errors do not hide the failing step. It prints no `gh` watch or force-cancel recipe; the running `yoke qa case run` invocation is the watch. The gate itself force-cancels a run that never starts and redispatches it, and a stalled-dispatch detail and the cancel refusal say so. Observed in source and tests; deployed proof is pending. Jobs with failure, startup_failure or cancelled conclusions and no runner or steps reached no verdict. The failed-log report labels them never_started and reads Checks annotations instead of downloading nonexistent logs. Watchers and CI QA preserve annotation levels and messages. A failure annotation asks the operator before any retry and does not spend a no-verdict attempt; without annotations the existing retry remains. A nonzero runner_id proves a job started even with no steps; its missing or expired log stays expired_or_missing.
